los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the hip with increased confidence and accuracy.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LO 10 (look including gait and Trendelenburg; leg lengths; feel; move including internal rotation; Thomas's test).
Accuracy tips
Measure true leg length from ASIS to medial malleolus
Stabilise the pelvis with a hand on the opposite ASIS during abduction/adduction
Internal rotation at 90° hip flexion is the first movement lost in OA
Finish with knee and lumbar spine and say why

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform a competent examination of the CVS/Resp system
los.html:
• Routines: CVS (ICM Year 1 › Cardiovascular › LO 1), respiratory (ICM Year 1 › Respiratory › LO 2).
    • Competence = fluent sequence, correct technique, checking the patient's comfort, and finishing steps.

los.text: Interpret and integrate findings with relevant knowledge to support clinical reasoning
los.html:
IntegrateExample
Signs that fit togetherIrregular pulse + raised JVP + basal crackles + ankle oedema → AF with congestive heart failure
Explain whyRaised venous pressure from right heart failure → oedema
Next testsECG, echo, BNP, CXR, U&E
Respiratory exampleClubbing + fine bibasal crackles → pulmonary fibrosis → HRCT, spirometry (restrictive)

los.text: Clearly present these findings to peers or supervisors.
los.html:
• Present: introduce the patient and the exam, positive findings, relevant negatives, summary, most likely diagnosis and differentials, next steps.
    • Be concise and confident
    • answer questions honestly ("I'm not sure, but I would…").

los.text: Take a focused history from a confused patient and their carer, ensuring effective communication.
los.html:
Triadic consultationDo
IntroductionsBoth patient and carer; clarify relationships and roles
Speak to the patient first, involve them as much as possibleRespect autonomy
Carer for collateral historyOnset and course of confusion (acute = delirium), baseline function, medications, falls, eating/drinking
Check consent to share informationCapacity
Balance voicesMake sure the patient isn't talked over
  • Confusion history: acute vs chronic (delirium vs dementia), infection symptoms (urinary, chest), new medications, alcohol, pain, constipation, retention, sleep.

los.text: Explain the potential complications of the triadic consultation, including communication challenges and biases.
los.html:
ChallengeExample
Patient excludedCarer answers for them, loss of autonomy and dignity
Conflicting accountsPatient and carer disagree
ConfidentialityPatient may not want the carer to know some things
Hidden concernsCarer stress, safeguarding (abuse, neglect)
BiasesAssuming confusion = dementia; ageism; carer bias
Time and dynamicsTalking over, emotional tension
  • Strategies: speak to each separately if needed, check capacity, summarise both views, look for safeguarding cues.

los.text: Identify clinical signs indicative of infection during patient examination.
los.html:
SignSuggests
Fever, rigors, tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnoeaSystemic infection / sepsis
New confusionSepsis, especially in older people
Crackles, bronchial breathingPneumonia
Suprapubic or loin tenderness, dipstick nitritesUTI / pyelonephritis
Red, warm, swollen skinCellulitis
Neck stiffness, photophobia, rashMeningitis
New murmur, splinter haemorrhagesEndocarditis
Red, tender line siteLine infection

los.text: Use clinical reasoning to develop and justify a diagnosis based on patient history and examination findings.
los.html:
• Reasoning: list key findings (e.g. new confusion, fever, suprapubic tenderness, dipstick positive)
    • → generate a differential (delirium secondary to UTI vs pneumonia vs drug-related)
    • → test with investigations (urine culture, bloods, CXR)
    • → justify the most likely diagnosis and treat the cause.

los.text: Recognise and respond to patient cues related to self-harm and suicide, demonstrating appropriate communication and escalation.
los.html:
• Respond to self-harm cues (see ICM Year 1 › Mental health › LO 9): ask directly about suicidal thoughts
    • assess risk (plans, means, previous attempts, protective factors)
    • keep the patient safe
    • escalate to a senior or the mental health team
    • document.

los.text: Explain the rationale for conducting an ABCDE assessment and justify each step in the clinical context.
los.html:
StageRationale
AirwayObstruction kills within minutes
BreathingHypoxia kills next
CirculationShock and bleeding
DisabilityBrain function; glucose; drugs
ExposureHidden causes (rash, bleeding, DVT)
  • Why ABCDE: tackles the most immediately life-threatening problems first
    • gives a common language for teams
    • works when the diagnosis is unknown
    • and prompts reassessment after each intervention.
